newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates end down, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates end down, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistan's money rates slipped at the close on excess liquidity on Tuesday but could rise tomorrow when the State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) conducts its weekly open market operation, dealers said.
Overnight funds, initially traded at two percent, fell to one percent at the end, a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
Bids worth a total of 8.98 billion rupees were submitted in the auction of six-month federal bonds, the dealer said.
Bids ranged from 14.5 to 17.5 percent at a weighted average yield of 15.75 percent. The auction is to be settled on Thursday against maturity of T-bills worth 3.1 billion rupees, they said.
They expected rates to edge up on Wednesday in anticipation of acceptance of substantial amounts by the SBP in its OMO.
